frases.texto: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 3: The Sierra Morena and Princess Micomicona
frases.fala: Don Quixote of La Mancha. Part 3: The Sierra Morena and Princess Micomicona

frases.texto: With the shiny helmet he won in the rain and a heart full of dreams, the Knight of the Sorrowful Face climbs with Sancho up the high, wild mountains of the SIERRA MORENA!
frases.fala: With the shiny helmet he won in the rain and a heart full of dreams, the Knight of the Sorrowful Face climbs with Sancho up the high, wild mountains of the sierra morena!

frases.texto: Up there, among rocks, pine trees and wild flowers, the two friends will open a suitcase full of secrets, write a love LETTER, turn somersaults of longing and find out about a clever plan made by two old friends, with the help of a PRINCESS from a kingdom far, far away.
frases.fala: Up there, among rocks, pine trees and wild flowers, the two friends will open a suitcase full of secrets, write a love letter, turn somersaults of longing and find out about a clever plan made by two old friends, with the help of a princess from a kingdom far, far away.

frases.texto: Take a deep breath of the cool mountain air, turn the page and climb the mountains with them!
frases.fala: Take a deep breath of the cool mountain air, turn the page and climb the mountains with them!

frases.texto: Chapter 16. The Lost Suitcase. A Treasure in the Middle of the Mountains
frases.fala: Chapter 16. The Lost Suitcase. A Treasure in the Middle of the Mountains

frases.texto: Climbing the stony paths, between crooked trees and great walls of rock, Sancho tripped over a leather SUITCASE, forgotten under a prickly bush.
frases.fala: Climbing the stony paths, between crooked trees and great walls of rock, Sancho tripped over a leather suitcase, forgotten under a prickly bush.

frases.texto: The suitcase was old and wet from the rain, and its clasps were rusty.
frases.fala: The suitcase was old and wet from the rain, and its clasps were rusty.

frases.texto: What could be inside?
frases.fala: What could be inside?

frases.texto: Open the suitcase with a tap and find out the secret!
frases.fala: Open the suitcase with a tap and find out the secret!

frases.texto: Inside, lots of gold COINS were shining, and Sancho’s eyes went wide with joy.
frases.fala: Inside, lots of gold coins were shining, and Sancho’s eyes went wide with joy.

frases.texto: There was also a NOTEBOOK full of POEMS, written by hand in very neat writing.
frases.fala: There was also a notebook full of poems, written by hand in very neat writing.

frases.texto: “Gold, my lord!
frases.fala: Gold, my lord!

frases.texto: Real gold!” cheered Sancho, hopping up and down.
frases.fala: Real gold! cheered Sancho, hopping up and down.

frases.texto: Don Quixote picked up the notebook very carefully and read aloud the poems of a young man in love, who was wandering lost and sad in the mountains.
frases.fala: Don Quixote picked up the notebook very carefully and read aloud the poems of a young man in love, who was wandering lost and sad in the mountains.

frases.texto: “Anyone who writes with so much feeling has a noble heart,” said the knight, with a sigh.
frases.fala: Anyone who writes with so much feeling has a noble heart, said the knight, with a sigh.

frases.texto: “Books keep the most beautiful secrets of the heart!”
frases.fala: Books keep the most beautiful secrets of the heart!

frases.texto: Chapter 17. The Somersaults of Longing. A Knight Head over Heels
frases.fala: Chapter 17. The Somersaults of Longing. A Knight Head over Heels

frases.texto: Looking at those mountains, so big and so quiet, Don Quixote had an idea: “Friend Sancho, I shall stay here in this clearing to show the world my great LONGING for Dulcinea, and how much I miss her, just like AMADIS of Gaul, the hero of my books!
frases.fala: Looking at those mountains, so big and so quiet, Don Quixote had an idea: Friend Sancho, I shall stay here in this clearing to show the world my great longing for Dulcinea, and how much I miss her, just like amadis of Gaul, the hero of my books!

frases.texto: And you will ride your donkey and take a love letter right into her hands.”
frases.fala: And you will ride your donkey and take a love letter right into her hands.

frases.texto: “But, my lord,” asked Sancho, scratching his chin, “how can I tell Lady Dulcinea that you nearly went bonkers from missing her, if I don’t see anything bonkers with my own eyes?”
frases.fala: But, my lord, asked Sancho, scratching his chin, how can I tell Lady Dulcinea that you nearly went bonkers from missing her, if I don’t see anything bonkers with my own eyes?

frases.texto: “Then look right now!” answered Don Quixote.
frases.fala: Then look right now! answered Don Quixote.

frases.texto: He took off his iron armour and, in just his long white nightshirt, turned a SOMERSAULT on the grass, with his skinny legs high up in the air!
frases.fala: He took off his iron armour and, in just his long white nightshirt, turned a somersault on the grass, with his skinny legs high up in the air!

frases.texto: Sancho covered his face with his hands and laughed so much that tears ran down his cheeks.
frases.fala: Sancho covered his face with his hands and laughed so much that tears ran down his cheeks.

frases.texto: Help the knight with his somersaults of longing!
frases.fala: Help the knight with his somersaults of longing!

frases.texto: Chapter 18. The Letter for Dulcinea. Sancho Forgot the Letter!
frases.fala: Chapter 18. The Letter for Dulcinea. Sancho Forgot the Letter!

frases.texto: With his heart beating fast, Don Quixote wrote a lovely LETTER to Dulcinea on a page torn out of the poem notebook, promising to love her for ever.
frases.fala: With his heart beating fast, Don Quixote wrote a lovely letter to Dulcinea on a page torn out of the poem notebook, promising to love her for ever.

frases.texto: Sancho climbed onto his donkey and set off down the road, feeling like the most important person in all of Spain!
frases.fala: Sancho climbed onto his donkey and set off down the road, feeling like the most important person in all of Spain!

frases.texto: But on the very first slope, Sancho put his hands in his pockets and his eyes went wide: he had left the letter on top of a rock, high up in the mountains!
frases.fala: But on the very first slope, Sancho put his hands in his pockets and his eyes went wide: he had left the letter on top of a rock, high up in the mountains!

frases.texto: He scratched his forehead and tried to remember the words he had kept only in his MEMORY: “How did it start again?
frases.fala: He scratched his forehead and tried to remember the words he had kept only in his memory: How did it start again?

frases.texto: ‘Most high and mighty lady’...
frases.fala: ‘Most high and mighty lady’...

frases.texto: That’s it!
frases.fala: That’s it!

frases.texto: And at the end?
frases.fala: And at the end?

frases.texto: How did he sign it again?”
frases.fala: How did he sign it again?

frases.texto: Help good Sancho remember the SIGNATURE on the letter by tapping the words in the right order!
frases.fala: Help good Sancho remember the signature on the letter by tapping the words in the right order!

frases.texto: Chapter 19. Friends in Disguise. The Priest, the Barber and an Ox-Tail Beard
frases.fala: Chapter 19. Friends in Disguise. The Priest, the Barber and an Ox-Tail Beard

frases.texto: When they stopped at the inn at the foot of the mountain, Sancho met two old friends from his village: the kind PRIEST Pero Pérez and Master Nicolás, the barber.
frases.fala: When they stopped at the inn at the foot of the mountain, Sancho met two old friends from his village: the kind priest Pero Pérez and Master Nicolás, the barber.

frases.texto: They were worried because Alonso Quixano had disappeared, so they had come to take him home, with lots of love.
frases.fala: They were worried because Alonso Quixano had disappeared, so they had come to take him home, with lots of love.

frases.texto: “He’ll never want to go home,” warned Sancho, “unless a young lady in danger asks his sword for help!”
frases.fala: He’ll never want to go home, warned Sancho, unless a young lady in danger asks his sword for help!

frases.texto: “I know!” said the priest, his eyes shining.
frases.fala: I know! said the priest, his eyes shining.

frases.texto: “Let’s make up a princess in danger!”
frases.fala: Let’s make up a princess in danger!

frases.texto: And so the two of them came up with a very clever plan: a DISGUISE!
frases.fala: And so the two of them came up with a very clever plan: a disguise!

frases.texto: Master Nicolás stuck a huge red BEARD on his chin, made from the hairy tail of an ox, and the priest put on a twirly skirt and a flowery bonnet over his priest’s clothes.
frases.fala: Master Nicolás stuck a huge red beard on his chin, made from the hairy tail of an ox, and the priest put on a twirly skirt and a flowery bonnet over his priest’s clothes.

frases.texto: When they looked in the mirror, all three of them burst out laughing and almost ran out of breath!
frases.fala: When they looked in the mirror, all three of them burst out laughing and almost ran out of breath!

frases.texto: Chapter 20. Princess Micomicona. A Princess Asks for Help
frases.fala: Chapter 20. Princess Micomicona. A Princess Asks for Help

frases.texto: To make the plan work, a young woman called Dorotea decided to help.
frases.fala: To make the plan work, a young woman called Dorotea decided to help.

frases.texto: She was clever, brave and very good at acting!
frases.fala: She was clever, brave and very good at acting!

frases.texto: Wearing a shiny silk dress and a velvet cloak, she climbed up the mountain and knelt down in front of Don Quixote:
frases.fala: Wearing a shiny silk dress and a velvet cloak, she climbed up the mountain and knelt down in front of Don Quixote:

frases.texto: “O brave knight, flower of all knights!” she begged in a sweet voice.
frases.fala: O brave knight, flower of all knights! she begged in a sweet voice.

frases.texto: “I am PRINCESS MICOMICONA, from the faraway kingdom of Micomicón!
frases.fala: I am princess micomicona, from the faraway kingdom of Micomicón!

frases.texto: A wicked giant, Pandafilando of the Gloomy Glare, has taken over my lands, and only you can save my people!”
frases.fala: A wicked giant, Pandafilando of the Gloomy Glare, has taken over my lands, and only you can save my people!

frases.texto: Deeply touched, Don Quixote held out his hand to the young woman and made a PROMISE: “Stand up, fair princess!
frases.fala: Deeply touched, Don Quixote held out his hand to the young woman and made a promise: Stand up, fair princess!

frases.texto: I swear by my sword that I shall beat that giant!”
frases.fala: I swear by my sword that I shall beat that giant!

frases.texto: And so, as happy as could be and without guessing a thing, the knight climbed onto Rocinante and took the road back home!
frases.fala: And so, as happy as could be and without guessing a thing, the knight climbed onto Rocinante and took the road back home!

frases.texto: Chapter 21. The Battle of the Wineskins. A Giant in the Middle of the Night
frases.fala: Chapter 21. The Battle of the Wineskins. A Giant in the Middle of the Night

frases.texto: Back at the inn, everyone was sleeping peacefully when battle cries woke up the whole house: “Give up, you wicked giant!
frases.fala: Back at the inn, everyone was sleeping peacefully when battle cries woke up the whole house: Give up, you wicked giant!

frases.texto: Now you’ll see!”
frases.fala: Now you’ll see!

frases.texto: It was Don Quixote, in his white nightshirt and still fast asleep, fighting the WINESKINS hanging on the bedroom wall: big leather bags full of red wine!
frases.fala: It was Don Quixote, in his white nightshirt and still fast asleep, fighting the wineskins hanging on the bedroom wall: big leather bags full of red wine!

frases.texto: In the middle of his DREAM, every wineskin looked like the terrible GIANT Pandafilando!
frases.fala: In the middle of his dream, every wineskin looked like the terrible giant Pandafilando!

frases.texto: Swinging his SWORD in the dark, he poked holes in the thick leather and made the wine run across the floor like a red river.
frases.fala: Swinging his sword in the dark, he poked holes in the thick leather and made the wine run across the floor like a red river.

frases.texto: Tap the sword and help the knight beat the wineskins!
frases.fala: Tap the sword and help the knight beat the wineskins!

frases.texto: “My wine!
frases.fala: My wine!

frases.texto: My wine!” cried the innkeeper, very upset.
frases.fala: My wine! cried the innkeeper, very upset.

frases.texto: “Calm down, my good man, I’ll pay for everything!” promised the priest.
frases.fala: Calm down, my good man, I’ll pay for everything! promised the priest.

frases.texto: And Don Quixote, very proud of himself, went back to bed and slept in peace, sure that he had saved Princess Micomicona’s kingdom!
frases.fala: And Don Quixote, very proud of himself, went back to bed and slept in peace, sure that he had saved Princess Micomicona’s kingdom!

frases.texto: Chapter 22. Arms and Letters. Stories at the Inn
frases.fala: Chapter 22. Arms and Letters. Stories at the Inn

frases.texto: That night, the big room at the inn filled up with travellers, merchants and families around a large table lit by candles.
frases.fala: That night, the big room at the inn filled up with travellers, merchants and families around a large table lit by candles.

frases.texto: Warm bread was passed from hand to hand, and everyone told their STORIES: adventures at sea, surprise meetings and old legends from all over the world.
frases.fala: Warm bread was passed from hand to hand, and everyone told their stories: adventures at sea, surprise meetings and old legends from all over the world.

frases.texto: Then Don Quixote stood up at the end of the table and gave a wise and beautiful speech about the ARMS of knights, their swords and shields, and the LETTERS of books: “The courage of knights keeps the peace and protects those who are weaker.
frases.fala: Then Don Quixote stood up at the end of the table and gave a wise and beautiful speech about the arms of knights, their swords and shields, and the letters of books: The courage of knights keeps the peace and protects those who are weaker.

frases.texto: And books, my friends, make justice, truth and beauty grow in our hearts!”
frases.fala: And books, my friends, make justice, truth and beauty grow in our hearts!

frases.texto: Everyone looked at one another, amazed at how wise that dreamy knight was.
frases.fala: Everyone looked at one another, amazed at how wise that dreamy knight was.

frases.texto: The priest and the barber smiled, deeply touched: it was time to take their dear friend back to his cosy home!
frases.fala: The priest and the barber smiled, deeply touched: it was time to take their dear friend back to his cosy home!

mi... co... mi... co... na... micomicona!
